transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today, and what would you like help with?

I just don’t enjoy anything anymore, even the stuff I used to really like, and it’s been that way for a long time now. I feel like I’m just going through the motions and it’s starting to affect everything, so I thought I should get some help.
How long have you been feeling this way without a real break—are we talking weeks, months, or years, and do these feelings ever fully lift for a while or are they there almost all the time?
It’s been going on for about nine months now. It’s there pretty much all the time—some days are a bit less heavy than others, but it never really goes away or feels back to normal.
Over these past nine months, have you also been feeling persistently anxious or worried about many different things most days, or is it mainly the low mood and loss of interest that bother you?

It’s mainly the low mood and not enjoying anything that really bother me. I do worry sometimes, but it doesn’t feel like constant anxiety—mostly it’s just this heavy, flat feeling that doesn’t let up.

Because of this low mood and loss of interest, how much has your ability to function in daily life been affected—for example with work or school, taking care of yourself, and relationships: only a little, quite a lot, or so much that you’re barely managing or not managing at all?

I’d say it’s affected me quite a lot, maybe close to barely managing some days. At work I’m really slow, miss deadlines, and just stare at the screen instead of getting things done. At home I let dishes and laundry pile up and often skip showers, and I’ve been avoiding friends and not replying to messages much anymore.

Before these past nine months, have you ever had a similar period of at least a couple of weeks where you felt this low and lost interest in things, or is this the first time it’s been like this for you?

I’ve had times in the past where I felt down for a week or two, like after a breakup or stress at work, but it always passed and I could still enjoy things. This is the first time it’s been this intense and gone on this long without really lifting.

Over these nine months, have you also had problems like major changes in sleep or appetite, feeling slowed down or restless, trouble concentrating or making decisions, or strong feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt—and if so, which of these have been most noticeable for you?

Yeah, a lot of that. My sleep is all over the place—some nights I can’t fall asleep for hours, other times I wake up a lot or way too early and can’t get back to sleep, and even when I sleep in I wake up exhausted and have a lot of bad dreams. I’m either really slowed down, like moving and talking feels heavy, or I’m pacing around, and I keep getting stuck in my head about how useless I am and replaying little mistakes from years ago and feeling like everything bad is somehow my fault.

With how low and guilty you’ve been feeling, have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, that you’d be better off dead, or any thoughts about harming yourself—even if you wouldn’t act on them?
I’m not sure how to answer that, I haven’t really thought about it in that way.
Do you ever find yourself wishing you wouldn’t wake up in the morning or thinking that life doesn’t feel worth living anymore, even if you haven’t made any plans to harm yourself?

Yeah, I do sometimes think it wouldn’t be so bad if I just didn’t wake up, like it’d be a relief not to have to deal with anything anymore. It’s more this feeling that life doesn’t really feel worth much right now than actually planning to do something to myself.

Over the past month or so, have your symptoms made it impossible to work, study, or manage basic daily tasks so that you’ve had to stop or take leave, or are you still managing to keep going, even if it feels very hard and you’re doing much less than before?

I’m still going, but it feels like I’m just barely keeping up. I haven’t taken leave, but I’m a lot slower and less productive at work, and at home I only do the bare minimum—most chores and errands just get put off until I absolutely have to deal with them.

Over these months, how much trouble have you had thinking clearly, focusing, or making even simple decisions—does it feel noticeably harder than before, and does it get in the way of getting things done?

Yeah, it’s definitely harder than before. I lose my train of thought really easily and can end up rereading the same email or document over and over without taking it in, and even simple choices like what to eat or what task to start can feel weirdly overwhelming and make me just freeze.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has had a persistent depressive episode for about nine months with nearly continuous low mood, marked anhedonia, sleep disturbance, psychomotor changes, impaired concentration/decision-making, and feelings of worthlessness/guilt, along with passive death wishes. Functioning is clearly impaired at work and at home, but the patient remains able to continue working and manage basic tasks, albeit at a reduced level. This pattern meets criteria for a single episode of moderate depressive disorder (F32.1). It does not reach the threshold for severe depressive episode (F32.2), as there is no evidence of psychotic symptoms and the functional impairment, while substantial, has not rendered the patient unable to work or manage basic self-care.
